mcqs.question: A convex lens has a focal length of 25 cm. What is its power in dioptres?
mcqs.explanation: Power (P) of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length (f) in metres: P = 1/f. Here f = 25 cm = 0.25 m, so P = 1/0.25 = 4 dioptres. Options A, C and D give incorrect reciprocals.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: A converging lens of power +6 D is placed in contact with a diverging lens of power -2 D. What is the net power of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: When thin lenses are in contact, their powers add algebraically: P_total = P1 + P2 = (+6) + (‑2) = +4 D. Option A adds the absolute values, C subtracts incorrectly, and D would be correct only if the powers were equal and opposite.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: With Cartesian signs, object distance u = –30 cm, focal length f = +10 cm. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v – 1/u. Substituting, 1/10 = 1/v – (‑1/30) → 1/v = 1/10 – 1/30 = 2/30 = 1/15, so v = +15 cm (real image on the opposite side). Options B, C, and D arise from sign or algebra errors.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 12 cm to the left of a diverging lens whose focal length is –20 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: For a diverging lens, f = –20 cm; object distance u = –12 cm. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v – 1/u → 1/(‑20) = 1/v – (‑1/12) → –1/20 = 1/v + 1/12 → 1/v = –1/20 – 1/12 = –(3+5)/60 = –8/60 = –2/15, so v = –7.5 cm. The negative sign indicates a virtual image on the same side as the object. Options B, C, D ignore sign or mis‑calculate.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length +15 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm from the lens. A concave lens of focal length –15 cm forms an image of the same object placed at the same distance. Which lens produces the larger magnitude of magnification?

options.C: Both lenses produce the same magnitude

mcqs.explanation: For the convex lens: 1/15 = 1/v – (‑1/30) → v = +30 cm, magnification m = v/u = 30/(‑30) = –1 (|m| = 1). For the concave lens: 1/(‑15) = 1/v – (‑1/30) → v = –10 cm, m = (‑10)/(‑30) = 1/3 (|m| = 0.33). The convex lens therefore gives the larger magnitude of magnification. Options B, C, D are incorrect based on the calculations.

mcqs.question: The power of a lens is defined as:

options.A: The ability of a lens to converge or diverge light measured in dioptres.
options.B: The reciprocal of its focal length in metres.
options.C: The product of its focal length and the refractive index of the material.
options.D: The ratio of image distance to object distance.

mcqs.answer: The reciprocal of its focal length in metres.
mcqs.explanation: Power (P) = 1/f, where f is the focal length in metres; the unit is dioptre (D). Option A describes the effect but not the definition, C mixes unrelated quantities, and D describes magnification, not power.

mcqs.question: What is the power of a lens whose focal length is 0.5 m?
mcqs.explanation: Power P = 1/f. With f = 0.5 m, P = 1/0.5 = 2 dioptres. The other options correspond to incorrect reciprocals.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: Two thin lenses in contact have powers of +3 D and +5 D. What is the resultant power of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: For thin lenses in contact, powers add: P_total = +3 D + +5 D = +8 D. Option A subtracts, C multiplies, and D would be correct only if the powers were equal and opposite.
